title: Shift and Enter
summary: Capitals with the opposite little finger, and the line break.
intro: Everything so far has been lower case. Shift changes that, and it has one rule worth getting right from the start: the little finger of the hand opposite the letter presses it. With the same little finger the hand twists and you end up looking at the keyboard.
congrats: With Shift and Enter you can type a whole piece of text the way it is written outside this course.

screens.text: Capitals come from the little finger of the hand opposite the letter. Hold Shift, press the letter, let go. Never with the same little finger that types it.
screens.hint: Hold Shift and press a letter to continue

screens.text: Capitals and lower case, alternating. The little finger goes down and up; the other hand does not move.
screens.content:
Qq Nn Zz Hh
Ww Ss Vv Oo
Ll Pp Ee Uu
Xx Kk Tt Bb

screens.text: Words with a capital at the front, the way names are written.
screens.content:
french shag east glide
lady age door heal
we upper ugly school

screens.text: Enter belongs to your right little finger, to the right of the home row. It is the biggest key that finger has to reach.
A line, Enter, the next line. The little finger goes out and back without dragging the hand along.
screens.content:
Petra
Ali
Ruth
Nadia
Noah
Paul

screens.text: Sentences with a capital at the start and a period at the end. This is starting to look like real writing.
screens.content:
Be quick but do not be careless.
They are still here.
The story is worth it.

screens.text: A burst to settle what this lesson taught.
Five to a line, with the little finger working in both directions.
screens.content:
wasn't notes grid excellent kept
only will house birds title
long wild stood entire give

screens.text: Whole sentences to finish. Shift, letter, release — without stopping to think about it.
screens.content:
You can learn this in one hour.
You'll get there one line at a time.
The question is simple enough.
